run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The only object changed after the namespace was installed and before the load test started is the frontend-proxy Deployment: it was rolled to revision 2 at 21:47:30 (new ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-88764bfbb, old Envoy pod frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-xsnpm stopped at 21:47:32) with the same image digest but a different container command - a hand-written single-threaded Perl 'edge request filter' run with WAF_RULE_ENABLED=true and WAF_RULE_REGEX=^([a-zA-Z]+)*$, and a 100m CPU limit. That regex is a nested-quantifier pattern prone to catastrophic backtracking, the script evaluates the user-supplied waf query parameter against it on every request, answers any request with a non-empty waf parameter with a synthetic 200 'ok' that never reaches the frontend, returns 502 'bad gateway' when the frontend connect fails, and its visible code exports no spans or metrics (Envoy, which produced the 'GET/POST' and 'router frontend egress' spans, is no longer the process). This is the fault-injecting setting in effect on the just-rolled workload, and no other object is seen applying a change or fault to it, so the Deployment is named as root cause. The 500-error burst seen in the window is NOT from that change: frontend-proxy's and frontend's error spans all trace to frontend gRPC '14 UNAVAILABLE ... connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.146.209:8080' (product-catalog's ClusterIP) while product-catalog was still waiting for postgresql until 21:47:03, and frontend requests were served normally (200s in 5-13 ms) at 21:47:31-32 after that dependency came up. The 30-67 s checkout latencies seen after the rollout also cannot be attributed to it: the same magnitudes were already present at 21:47:24-26, before the rollout (comparable baseline). Because the declared fault (a request actually being stalled by the rule, or a waf-parameter bypass happening) was not itself observed - only 10 s of load ran before the window closed - the conclusion is partial. Checked and healthy: all 24 astronomy-shop Deployments had available == ready, all 27 pods were Running/Ready with 0 restarts, no NetworkPolicy objects exist at query time, the Kafka cluster showed 0 under-replicated/offline partitions, and every flagd demo fault flag was off in flagd-config.

claims.text: All 27 astronomy-shop pods were Running with all containers ready, restartCount 0 and no last-terminated state (including frontend-proxy-88764bfbb-mfd8h, created 21:47:30).

Deployment astronomy-shop/frontend-proxy is at deployment revision 2 with command [/usr/bin/perl -e] and an inline edge-filter script, env WAF_RULE_REGEX=^([a-zA-Z]+)*$ and WAF_RULE_ENABLED=true, resources.limits.cpu=100m, while the image is unchanged (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy).

The previous frontend-proxy template (ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5, revision 1) started Envoy via '/bin/sh -c envsubst < envoy.tmpl.yaml ... && exec envoy -c envoy.yaml', had no WAF variables and only a memory limit (65Mi), i.e. the change is configuration-only with an identical image digest.

Events show Deployment frontend-proxy scaling seat frontend-proxy-88764bfbb from 0 to 1 at 21:47:30, the old ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 from 1 to 0 at 21:47:32 and pod frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-xsnpm being killed at 21:47:32, with the replacement container created 21:47:31 and started 21:47:31.

The replaced container's logs are Envoy's ('caught ENVOY_SIGTERM' and 'exiting' at 21:47:32, 'all dependencies initialized. starting workers' at 21:46:45, 'instantiating a new tracer: envoy.tracers.opentelemetry'), confirming Envoy was the proxy process before the rollout.

The replacement script's visible code reads the request line, headers and Content-Length body, extracts the query parameter 'waf', evaluates it against WAF_RULE_REGEX whenever WAF_RULE_ENABLED is not 'false' (it is set to 'true'), returns a synthetic 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK ... ok' for any non-empty waf parameter without contacting the upstream, otherwise forwards to FRONTEND_HOST:8080, and answers '502 Bad Gateway' if the upstream connect fails; the visible script contains no OTLP span or metric export.

Frontend-proxy spans carried 32 STATUS_CODE_ERROR and 32 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans (cumulative at 21:47:46), and the frontend spans returned for 21:40:00-21:47:46 start between 21:47:19.03 and 21:47:29.19 with http.status_code 500 on GET/POST and 'router frontend egress' operations.

frontend spans carried 91 STATUS_CODE_ERROR of 197 spans, and the frontend container logged repeated '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.146.209:8080' lines from 21:46:48 to 21:47:26; Service product-catalog has ClusterIP 10.96.146.209.

Traces show the 500 chain as load-generator POST 500 -> frontend-proxy POST 'router frontend egress' 500 -> frontend 'POST /api/checkout' 500 whose child oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct failed with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and the exception message 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.146.209:8080'.

The product-catalog pod's log shows its init container 'wait-for-postgresql' printing 'waiting for postgresql' from 21:46:52 to 21:47:01 and 'postgresql (10.96.9.17:5432) open' at 21:47:03, i.e. product-catalog was unavailable at the start of the window because its own dependency was not yet up.

After the proxy swap, frontend requests were served successfully: in the traces returned for 21:47:30-21:47:46 the frontend spans (GET /api/data 12.6 ms, GET /api/cart 6.2 ms, GET /api/products/{productId} 5.9 ms, GET /api/data 14.6 ms/308) between 21:47:31.27 and 21:47:32.03 all carry http.status_code 200/308, and none of those traces contains a frontend-proxy span.

Before the rollout, at 21:47:24.2-21:47:26.6, load-generator user_checkout_single spans already lasted 65.4 s and 67.0 s and their edge POST spans 42.8 s and 43.7 s while the matching frontend-proxy POST span lasted 41.2 ms; in the same period user_add_to_cart was 33.1 ms, load-generator POST 18.9 ms and frontend-proxy egress at most 26.5 ms.

After the rollout, load-generator checkout flows started 21:47:33-21:47:36 lasted 60.7-64.2 s and their POST spans to the edge 32.6 s, with the child frontend 'POST /api/checkout' handled in 38-52 ms with status 200; these magnitudes match the pre-rollout values rather than exceeding them.
All 24 astronomy-shop Deployments had kube_deployment_status_replicas_available minus replicas_ready equal to 0 at every 15 s sample from 21:47:30 to 21:47:45.

The frontend-proxy Service resolves to exactly one endpoint, 10.244.234.164:8080 backed by pod frontend-proxy-88764bfbb-mfd8h, whose labels match the Service selector opentelemetry.io/name=frontend-proxy.

In ConfigMap flagd-config every demo fault flag has defaultVariant 'off' (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad, failedReadinessProbe, emailMemoryLeak, llmRateLimitError, llmInaccurateResponse).
The API server returned no NetworkPolicy objects for the whole cluster at query time, and the Kafka cluster reported 1 broker, 2 topics, 51 partitions, 0 under-replicated and 0 offline partitions.

The locust-fetcher pod logged 'Running Locust on round #1' at 21:47:36.28 and a stats line at 21:47:36.29 with fail_ratio 0.375 and HTTP 500 errors on /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM, /api/products/LS4PSXUNUM and /api/checkout; the line does not state when those requests were issued.

The frontend-proxy Deployment revision 2 is the injected fault: a configuration-only rollout that replaced Envoy with a single-threaded Perl edge filter whose WAF rule ^([a-zA-Z]+)*$ is evaluated against attacker/user-controlled query input (catastrophic backtracking) and whose non-empty-waf branch answers 200 'ok' without forwarding, so edge traffic can be stalled or short-circuited and the proxy stops emitting its own OTLP spans/metrics; the change was applied at 21:47:30, six seconds before load round #1, and no other object is seen modifying the workload.

Requests that carry a non-empty 'waf' query parameter through frontend-proxy:8080 are answered by the Perl shim with a synthetic 200 'ok' and never reach the frontend, which would break those user journeys without any trace or error signal, and a long letter sequence followed by a non-letter would make the single listener thread backtrack exponentially under the 100m CPU limit; neither behaviour was directly observed in the window.

The window's 500 errors are explained by product-catalog being unreachable during startup, not by the frontend-proxy change: 10.96.146.209 is product-catalog's ClusterIP, product-catalog only opened its postgresql connection at 21:47:03, and frontend requests were answered 200 in 5-13 ms at 21:47:31-32.

The observed 30-67 s checkout/edge latency is not attributable to the frontend-proxy rollout: the same 65.4 s / 67.0 s user_checkout_single durations and 42.8 s / 43.7 s edge POST durations were already present at 21:47:24-21:47:26, before the new ReplicaSet existed, and the post-rollout values (60.7-64.2 s and 32.6 s) are of the same order.

Workload health was otherwise clean: all pods Running/Ready with 0 restarts, every Deployment available == ready, no NetworkPolicy objects, and all flagd demo fault flags off, so no other fault-injection setting or workload-level outage was found.

product-catalog unavailability is rejected as the root cause of an injected incident: it is explained by its own init container waiting for postgresql (open at 21:47:03) during a fresh namespace install, its pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, and successful product-catalog GetProduct spans (1.3 ms) return at 21:47:31.

The frontend-proxy rollout is rejected as the cause of the observed checkout latency, because a comparable baseline of the same operation before the rollout already showed 65-67 s user flows and 42-44 s edge POSTs.

Roll frontend-proxy back to the revision-1 Envoy template (or restore an equivalent proxy) and replace the ^([a-zA-Z]+)*$ check with a linear-time validation that cannot backtrack; do not answer a failed or bypassed filter match with a synthetic 200 'ok', and keep the proxy instrumented with OTLP so the edge remains observable.

Reproduce the edge path in a controlled way: send a request with a long non-letter 'waf' value to frontend-proxy:8080 and watch the container CPU and request latency, and confirm that a normal 'waf' value returns the shim's 'ok' body instead of the shop page.

gaps: The declared fault itself was not observed: no request is seen hitting the waf evaluation path and no 502 or stall from the Perl shim is observed; the window ended 16 s after the new pod started and the load round only began at 21:47:36.

The replacement pod's stdout is empty in both direct log reads and Loki ('Perl buffers stdout when it is not a terminal'), so the script's own 'request_filter_eval' lines and listening banner were not available.

traces_span_metrics_calls_total has only one sample inside the window (21:47:46), so no span-rate, error-rate or latency trend could be computed; a query for increase() over 20 minutes returned nothing and no other rpc_/http_/app_ metric series exist in this target.

No data was returned by the queries for frontend traces in 21:47:36-21:47:46, for frontend spans tagged error=true in 21:47:32-21:47:46, or for frontend log lines containing 'error' in 21:47:27-21:47:46; these are unmatched queries, not proof that the frontend was free of errors.

The runtime flag state served by flagd (which the flagd-ui sidecar can change without touching ConfigMap flagd-config) could not be verified beyond the ConfigMap defaults, and no secret value was readable.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what applied frontend-proxy revision 2 and the exact change time beyond the 21:47:30 event could not be established.

The three otel-collector-agent DaemonSet pods on the worker nodes were replaced between 21:47:15 and 21:47:20 and their logs contain kubeletstats TLS 'cannot validate certificate ... IP SANs' errors; why they were replaced and whether that affected collection was not determined, so it is recorded as an unexplained change in the window.
The Redis/Valkey tool returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so valkey-cart was not inspected directly; cart spans (valkey-cart:6379 sub-millisecond) are the only indication for that dependency.

Whether the load-generator's 500s recorded at 21:47:36.29 belong to the new load round or to earlier requests could not be determined from the log line, and corresponding frontend error spans were not returned.
next_steps: Review the applied Deployment spec and any rollout record for astronomy-shop/frontend-proxy revision 2 to confirm the WAF filter was the intended change.

Run a controlled probe against frontend-proxy:8080 with a long non-letter waf parameter and with a normal waf parameter, watching pod CPU throttling and response bodies, to confirm the ReDoS and bypass paths.

Once the proxy is restored, compare frontend and load-generator latency/error rates across several load rounds to establish whether checkout latency improves or is a separate, pre-existing client-side queueing issue.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

notes: Incomplete result (limit: 60 lines were returned, the limit; older lines in the window were not returned (Loki reports no total). Narrow the selector or line filters, shorten the window, or count with count_over_time).

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
